assessment.rationale: This simulation is mainly a transport experiment, not a CAS object type-binding design. It does support opaque forwarding in principle because it focuses on ordered message passing and per-hop forwarding promises, but the documents do not define unknown-codec object handling, safe non-parsing behavior, or type-binding evolution rules. So it is only a weak indirect fit to the scenario.
strengths: Clear transport boundary: it does not claim to replace other layers.
Per-hop forward/wait/refuse promises give some local accountability.
Opaque forwarding is at least conceptually compatible with transport-level relay.
weaknesses: Scenario fit is weak because the sim does not define CAS type-binding behavior.
No explicit promise vocabulary about payload conformance or unknown-type handling.
Mixed-version and partition recovery are already identified as fragility concerns, which hurts this scenario.
risks: Layer mismatch: transport ordering may distract from the actual type-binding problem.
Ring liveness and membership fragility could block durable forwarding of opaque objects.
Unknown-type safety is not specified, so peers may still make unsafe assumptions above the transport layer.
open_questions: Can the transport carry a CID and related claims without any peer needing to parse the unknown object type?
What exact promise is made when a peer forwards an opaque object it cannot validate semantically?
How does the ring behave when an unknown typed object reaches mixed-version or offline peers during recovery?
assessment.authority_boundary: Evidence only; does not settle PromiseGrid design.
